identity.name: Benzoic acid
identity.chemical_class: Aromatic monocarboxylic acid (benzenecarboxylic acid); weak-acid preservative

function.mechanism: Weak-acid preservative action is pH-dependent; benzoic acid is used to inhibit microbial growth in foods and beverages, with regulatory use as an antimicrobial and flavoring agent/adjuvant.
common_food_categories: foods using benzoates for antimicrobial preservation

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI from EFSA 2016 re-evaluation of benzoic acid and benzoates, expressed as benzoic acid.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported no genotoxicity concern and no carcinogenic indication in reviewed data, but modeled ADI exceedance in toddlers/children under brand-loyal and carry-over scenarios.

fda.notes: Within 21 CFR Part 184 (direct food substances affirmed as GRAS); used as antimicrobial and flavoring agent/adjuvant, with current usage maximum of 0.1% in food under GMP.

adi.basis: JECFA 2021 group ADI 0-20 mg/kg bw applies to benzoic acid and benzoate salts (as benzoic acid equivalents); previous 0-5 mg/kg bw withdrawn.

concerns.summary: A 2025 systematic review of mammalian-cell studies reported frequent cytogenotoxicity signals for preservatives including sodium benzoate (micronuclei/chromosomal effects), though study designs and doses were heterogeneous.
Recent rat studies (2025-2026) reported reproductive-axis and testicular/ovarian toxicity findings after sodium benzoate exposure, including hormonal disruption and apoptosis markers.

A 2026 in vitro study reported synergistic nephrotoxicity for benzoic-acid co-exposure with acesulfame K via CTNNB1/STAT3 signaling; this is mechanistic evidence and not direct population-level causality.
A 2025 childhood asthma case-control/metabolomics study found benzoic-acid-associated signals in a mixed-additive exposure context; additive-specific causality remains uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2016 concluded benzoic acid/benzoates did not raise a genotoxicity concern in the reviewed dataset.
EFSA 2016 reported available data did not indicate carcinogenic potential.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2016 found temporary group ADI exceedance in child scenarios; JECFA later raised the group ADI to 0-20 mg/kg bw in 2021, so benchmark choice changes exceedance interpretation.

risk_assessment.rationale: E210 remains authorized (EFSA/FDA/JECFA) but requires ADI-based risk management, with EFSA child-scenario exceedance findings and a growing experimental literature indicating potential endocrine/reproductive, renal, and cytogenotoxic concerns at certain exposures or in mixtures.
key_factors: EFSA temporary group ADI of 5 mg/kg bw/day with exceedance in toddler/child scenarios.
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 184.1021 with GMP and 0.1% current usage cap.
JECFA 2021 group ADI update to 0-20 mg/kg bw (applies to benzoic acid/benzoates).
No direct IARC benzoic-acid listing found in current IARC classification dataset.
Recent mechanistic/animal studies report adverse signals, but many are high-dose or mixed-exposure designs.
